name: subdivide_dirty_parity
face_ring_start_note: Subdivision emits one face per corner of every source face, and measured 2026-08-18 the two engines start those rings at different corners on most of them (141 of 234 rings). The five cases where every ring agrees declare "compared" one by one below. What a subdivided quad's ring start should be is an unread law -- doc/tasks/backlog/1311-ring-start-laws-to-capture.md.
description: Faceted, smooth and Catmull-Clark subdivision of dirty bases: saddles, twists, reflex rings, collinear corners, holes, T-junctions, slivers, spirals and a six-point star.

provenance.notes: Applied to open surfaces with boundaries, which is where the boundary rule of a subdivision scheme actually shows: on a closed solid there is no boundary and every scheme's boundary clause is unreachable. One cell subdivides TWICE, so a scheme that is right once and wrong on its own output is caught. CHANNELS: the sweep's comparison was never vertex-only -- it compared the vertex multiset, the edge multiset, faces BOTH as ordered rings (winding shows) and as unordered position sets, the material partition, the per-face 'did this face's own tag change', and the post-command selection. Re-checked independently over all 215 frozen cases: ZERO agree on vertices while differing on ordered face rings, so nothing frozen here is a vertex-channel-only agreement. PRECISION: the sweep compared at 1e-4 and this fixture's tolerance matches it. The actual reproduction is far tighter -- 208 of the 215 cases are bit-identical at the dumps' 6 decimals and the remaining 7 agree to 3e-6 or better, that being the worst deviation anywhere in the set. The tolerance is the MEASUREMENT's bound, not the data's.
